svg.title: SteuerEule — Persistence Data Model · arc42 §5 (data view)

g.text: SteuerEule — Persistence Data Model · arc42 §5 (data view)
green = added since the REQ-001 revision (Slice 2 auth · REQ-011 Löschschutz)
better-auth identity (ADR-0009 · schema owned by the library)
userId is a logical scoping key on the domain tables, not a DB foreign key
(ADR-0007). Profile / TaxDataAccessLog / TaxYear / LegalHold carry no FK to
User: the same column holds either a
, and only the UserContextGuard decides which. Every
row is read scoped to a single userId; there are no cross-user joins.
The better-auth tables below *do* use real FKs among themselves.
steuerId / steuernummer are field-encrypted at rest
Plain facts only otherwise — clean side of the
On account deletion the row is hard-deleted
the ciphertext is genuinely gone, not soft-flagged. The
field-encryption key is app-wide, so per-user crypto-shredding
is not available — hard-delete is what makes erasure real.
Who/what/when only — no value column, never the plaintext
or ciphertext. Audited surface is identifier-class access
On account deletion the rows are anonymised, not deleted
(ADR-0013 §1): userId is re-keyed to an irreversible
`deleted:<uuid>` tombstone, so the processing record survives
while the person-link does not (Recital 26). That UPDATE is
ADR-014/048), so there is no second place to drift.
No @encrypted field: ruled out of ADR-0008 scope (Musti
review, R1a) — no tax identifier, only a rounded estimate
and two counts. Revisit if assessed amounts / income land here.
While holdUntil is in the future, the deletion transaction
and retains it under legal obligation. Today only "profile" /
"auditLog" are meaningful and the exempt set is vacuous in real
use — the mechanism is real and acceptance-tested on both
branches, so the UI's retention promise is not a hypothetical.
Deleting this row is what makes an account
Account cascade, Verification rows are removed by email, and the
whole teardown runs inside the single deletion $transaction
(ADR-0013 §3) together with Profile's hard-delete and the audit
providers) — no hash, no session/verification token, ever
an in-memory counter resets per pod and is trivially bypassed once
the API scales horizontally. Reused — not re-invented — by the
deletion path's password re-verification limit (ADR-0013 §6 note).
